newsitem.title: CHINA: S&P raises Hopewell outlook to stable.
newsitem.headline: S&P raises Hopewell outlook to stable.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Friday it has affirmed its BBB-minus corporate credit rating on Hopewell Holdings Ltd and revised the outlook to stable from negative.
S&P said the Hong Kong-based infrastructure and property developer has made positive changes in both its business and financial profile over the last 18 months.
The negative outlook was attributable to Hopewell's large leverage position, significant future equity commitments, and additional unplanned investments, S&P said.

But it said Hopewell's sale of Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd (CEPA) positioned it to better balance future capital expenditures as well as repay nearly US$1.9 billion of bank debt and other liabilities, reducing its consolidated leverage to 27 percent as of March 31, 1997, from 50 percent at June 30, 1996.

The rating agency said the outlook for Hopewell is stable upon the company's implementation of a strategy of reduced leverage and better focus on management of its existing portfolio and future investment portfolio.

S&P said it did not anticipate a downgrade over the next several years as cash flow to the holding company was projected to come primarily from real estate operations and to provide adequate debt service coverage for holding company debt.
The cash flow from Hopewell's two main Hong Kong properties -- Hopewell Centre and Panda Kowloon Hotel -- to be relatively stable.

But because of uncertainty remained as to the future development of both Bangkok Elevated Rail Transist System and Tanjung Jati B power plant in Indonesia, there was not much potential for any upgrade in the rating until the uncertainties were removed, the rating agency said.
